mainTopic: The sources for טעם כעיקר and היתר מצטרף לאיסור. רבי עקיבא learns from גיעולי גוים, the רבנן learn from ״משרת״, and the two sides argue over the rule of שני כתובים הבאין כאחד.
overview: The amud opens with רבי עקיבא's source for טעם כעיקר. He learns it from גיעולי גוים: the vessels taken from מדין held only absorbed taste, yet they had to be purged. The רבנן don't learn from there, because they see the law as a חידוש. It forbids even a spoiling taste, and even a pot used that same day spoils the taste a little. For רבי עקיבא the Torah forbade only a קדירה בת יומא, whose taste is good, so it is no חידוש. Next, רב אחא asks why רבי עקיבא's lesson from ״משרת״, that היתר מצטרף לאיסור, doesn't spread to the whole Torah. רב אשי answers that נזיר and חטאת are שני כתובים הבאין כאחד, and the גמרא brings the ברייתא on ״בבשרה יקדש״ as the חטאת source. The רבנן and רבי עקיבא then argue over whether both verses are needed and what each one teaches. Finally, רב כהנא explains that permitted food joins with forbidden food only when they are eaten together, but two forbidden foods join even one after the other. The amud ends as the גמרא starts a question about רבי שמעון, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns the rule from the gentiles' vessels
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא learns טעם כעיקר from גיעולי גוים. The vessels hold only absorbed taste, yet the Torah forbids them until they are purged, so taste counts like the real food everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from the non-Jews' vessels that need purging. The Torah says: "Every thing that passes through the fire," meaning these vessels are forbidden. Those vessels hold only taste, and still they are forbidden. Here too, it is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering where רבי עקיבא gets the rule of טעם כעיקר. He gets it from the vessels taken in the war with מדין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pot that cooked non-kosher food has no actual non-kosher food in it, only absorbed taste. Even so, the Torah requires purging it before use. That shows taste alone is enough to forbid, so רבי עקיבא applies this to all of the Torah's food laws.

keyTerms.meaning: Non-Jews' cooking vessels that must be purged of absorbed non-kosher taste
The taste of a forbidden food counts like the food itself
'The Merciful One', a name for ה׳ as giver of the Torah
It is no different

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a major source for the idea that absorbed taste can make food forbidden. That idea is the basis for the laws of הכשר כלים.

phrases.english: He derives it from the non-Jews' vessels that need purging,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי עקיבא, and 'it' is the rule that taste counts like the food itself.

phrases.english: as the Merciful One said:
"Every thing that passes through the fire"
that is to say that they are forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: גִּיעוּלֵי גוֹיִם לָאו טַעְמָא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא
phrases.english: The non-Jews' vessels: isn't that just mere taste?
And yet it is forbidden.
Here too, it is no different.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means all the other food prohibitions in the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question of where רבי עקיבא learns טעם כעיקר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא learns טעם כעיקר from the requirement to purge גיעולי גוים, since those vessels contain only taste.

steps.title: Why don't the רבנן also learn it from the vessels?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the רבנן need a different source when they could also learn טעם כעיקר from גיעולי גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the רבנן too, let them learn it from the non-Jews' vessels!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the רבנן. If the vessels prove the rule so well, why don't the רבנן use this source too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן learn טעם כעיקר from a different פסוק about the נזיר. If גיעולי גוים already proves the rule, that other source should not be needed for it. The question pushes us to find a weakness in the vessels as a proof.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion
Let them derive it from

phrases.english: And according to the Rabbis too,
let them derive it from the non-Jews' vessels!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבָּנַן נָמֵי תִּיפּוֹק לְהוּ מִגִּיעוּלֵי גוֹיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רבי עקיבא's source and asks why the רבנן don't use it too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's choice of a different source for טעם כעיקר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If גיעולי גוים clearly proves טעם כעיקר, a separate source is unnecessary.

steps.title: The vessels law is a one-time novelty
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that גיעולי גוים is a חידוש. Everywhere else a spoiling taste (נותן טעם לפגם) is permitted, but here even such a taste is forbidden, so no general rule can be learned from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, it is a novelty. Throughout the entire Torah, a taste that spoils the food is permitted, but for the non-Jews' vessels it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains why the רבנן won't learn from the vessels. The law of the vessels is unusual, so it cannot serve as a model for other cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, if a forbidden taste makes food worse, the food stays permitted. Vessels taken from non-Jews, which have usually sat unused for over a day so their taste is spoiled, are still forbidden. Because this law is stricter than the normal rule, it counts as a חידוש, and we don't build general rules from a חידוש.

keyTerms.meaning: A novelty: a law that breaks the normal pattern and cannot be applied elsewhere
Giving a taste that spoils the food
Permitted

steps.confusionAlert: נותן טעם לפגם does not mean no taste at all. There is a taste, but it makes the food worse, and the usual rule is that such a taste does not forbid the food.

phrases.english: He said to him: There, it is a novelty.
phrases.notes: רב אשי is answering רב אחא. 'There' means the law of the non-Jews' vessels.

phrases.english: For throughout the entire Torah,
something that gives a spoiling taste is permitted,
but regarding the non-Jews' vessels, it is forbidden.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source: it is a חידוש and cannot be applied to other cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: גיעולי גוים is a normal example that proves טעם כעיקר everywhere.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the vessels are forbidden even with a spoiling taste, the law is unusual, so the רבנן cannot learn from it.

steps.title: But for רבי עקיבא it is also a novelty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the same problem on רבי עקיבא. If the vessels law is a חידוש, how can he learn from it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי עקיבא too, this is a novelty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא with the same problem just raised for the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חידוש argument from step 3 seems to be a plain fact about the vessels. If so, רבי עקיבא should not be able to learn a general rule from them either, which seems to break his source in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: But this, used here to press a challenge

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Akiva too,
this is a novelty!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא נָמֵי הָא חִידּוּשׁ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the answer of step 3 and uses it against רבי עקיבא's source in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's derivation of טעם כעיקר from גיעולי גוים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חידוש cannot be applied elsewhere, so the vessels cannot be a source for a general rule.

steps.title: The Torah only forbade a same-day pot
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חייא answers that the Torah only forbade a קדירה בת יומא, a pot used within the last day. Its taste is still good, so the law is not a חידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חייא said: The Torah forbade only a pot used that same day, which does not give a spoiling taste.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר חייא defends רבי עקיבא. He explains that the Torah's ban on the vessels was never about a spoiling taste.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this answer, the Torah's ban covers only a pot used within the last day, whose absorbed taste still improves the food. That fits the normal rules, so the law is not a חידוש. It can therefore serve as a fair source for טעם כעיקר.

keyTerms.meaning: A pot used within the past day, whose absorbed taste is still fresh
The Torah forbade only

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא learns טעם כעיקר from גיעולי גוים because, in his view, the Torah only forbade a קדירה בת יומא, whose taste is not spoiled, so the law is not a חידוש. The רבנן see the law as a חידוש, since it forbids even a spoiling taste, so they don't learn from it.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of a בת יומא pot, whose absorbed taste is still fresh, becomes central in later כשרות discussions about used vessels.

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Chiya said:
The Torah forbade only
a pot used that same day,
phrases.notes: Literally 'a pot that is a daughter of the day', meaning it was cooked in within the past day.

phrases.english: which is not a case of giving a spoiling taste.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא: לֹא אָסְרָה תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא לִקְדֵירָה בַּת יוֹמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבי עקיבא in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the Torah's ban covers only a same-day pot
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Torah forbade the vessels even when their taste was spoiled, which would make the law a חידוש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban applies only to a קדירה בת יומא, whose taste is not spoiled, so the law follows normal rules and רבי עקיבא can learn from it.

steps.title: What do the רבנן say to the pot-of-the-day answer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the רבנן respond to רב הונא בר חייא's point that only a קדירה בת יומא was forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? Why don't they accept this and learn from גיעולי גוים?
steps.whatsHappening: In one word, the גמרא asks what the רבנן would say back to the answer we just heard. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא בר חייא showed that the vessels law is not a חידוש, because a pot used within the day still gives a good taste. If so, the רבנן should also be able to learn טעם כעיקר from it. The גמרא wants to know why they don't.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Rabbis? A short way of asking how the other side answers.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: Short for: why don't the רבנן also learn from גיעולי גוים, now that it isn't a חידוש?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רב הונא בר חייא's defense of רבי עקיבא back onto the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's refusal to learn טעם כעיקר from גיעולי גוים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a קדירה בת יומא gives a good taste, the vessels law is no חידוש, so the רבנן should be able to learn from it too.

steps.title: Even a pot from today spoils the taste a little
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold that even a pot used the same day must spoil the absorbed food slightly, so the vessels law is still a חידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even a pot used that same day cannot help but spoil the taste a little.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for the רבנן. Even a fresh pot always spoils the absorbed taste a bit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, any taste held inside a vessel is at least slightly spoiled, even within the day. So the Torah forbidding these vessels still means forbidding a spoiled taste, and that is a חידוש. Nothing general can be learned from it.

keyTerms.meaning: It spoils or damages the taste.
A little bit.
It is impossible.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: a pot from today gives good taste, so we can learn from גיעולי גוים. רבנן: even a pot from today spoils the taste a little, so גיעולי גוים stays a חידוש.

phrases.english: Even a pot used that day,
it is impossible that it does not spoil the taste a little.

steps.triggerLanguage: קְדֵירָה בַּת יוֹמָא נָמֵי אִי אֶפְשָׁר דְּלָא פָּגְמָה פּוּרְתָּא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual disagreement about whether a same-day pot spoils the taste
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A קדירה בת יומא gives a fully good taste, so גיעולי גוים is not a חידוש.
steps.terutzMaskana: For the רבנן, even a same-day pot spoils the taste slightly, so גיעולי גוים remains a חידוש.

steps.title: Why can't רבי עקיבא's rule from ״משרת״ apply to the whole Torah?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב אויא asks רב אשי: the רבנן spread their lesson from ״משרת״ to all of the Torah, so רבי עקיבא's lesson from ״משרת״, היתר מצטרף לאיסור, should spread to all of the Torah too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בריה דרב אויא said to רב אשי: Let us learn about רבי עקיבא from the רבנן. Don't the רבנן say that ״משרת״ teaches טעם כעיקר, and from there you learn it for every prohibition in the Torah? Then for רבי עקיבא too, who uses ״משרת״ to teach that a permitted food joins with a forbidden food, let us say that from there you learn it for every prohibition in the Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. If the רבנן spread their lesson from ״משרת״ to every prohibition, רבי עקיבא's lesson from the same word should spread to every prohibition too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that היתר מצטרף לאיסור works only for נזיר assumes that ״משרת״ teaches about נזיר alone. רב אחא points out that the רבנן don't limit the same word that way. He argues the two sides should be treated alike, so רבי עקיבא's rule should hold everywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: "Soaking", from the נזיר פסוק about grape soakings. It is the source both sides are reading.
A permitted food joins with a forbidden food to make up the amount needed for punishment.
From here you learn it for other cases.
Let us learn or infer.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַוְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rav Avya said to Rav Ashi:
From the Rabbis let us learn about Rabbi Akiva.
Don't the Rabbis say that this word "soaking"
is there to make taste count like the actual food,
and from here you learn
for all the prohibitions in the Torah?
For Rabbi Akiva too,
who uses this word "soaking"
to teach that permitted food joins with forbidden food,
let us say: from here you learn
for all the prohibitions in the Torah!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַוְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי מִדְּרַבָּנַן נִשְׁמַע לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from גיעולי גוים to whether רבי עקיבא's ״משרת״ lesson applies beyond נזיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that היתר מצטרף לאיסור applies only to נזיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן spread their ״משרת״ lesson to the whole Torah, so the same word should give רבי עקיבא's lesson the same wide reach.

steps.title: נזיר and חטאת are two verses teaching the same thing
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that היתר מצטרף לאיסור is taught in both נזיר and חטאת. Two verses that teach the same idea cannot be used for other cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because נזיר and חטאת are two verses that teach the same thing, and any two verses that teach the same thing do not teach for other cases.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains why רבי עקיבא's lesson stays limited to נזיר, using the rule of שני כתובים הבאין כאחד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah wanted a general rule, it would have written it once and we would apply it everywhere. Writing it twice, in נזיר and in חטאת, shows that the rule belongs only to those two cases. The רבנן's טעם כעיקר has no second verse, so it can spread.

keyTerms.meaning: Two verses that teach the same thing.
They do not teach a rule for other cases.
A sin-offering.

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards: two sources should make a rule stronger. But here the second verse is a sign that the rule is limited. Otherwise the Torah would not have needed to repeat it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why היתר מצטרף לאיסור stays limited to נזיר even though it comes from the same word that gives the רבנן a rule for the whole Torah.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב אשי answering רב אחא.

phrases.english: Because nazir and sin-offering are
two verses that come as one,
and any two verses that come as one
do not teach for other cases.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵי נָזִיר וְחַטָּאת שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִין הַבָּאִין כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's question in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out a difference: a rule taught twice cannot be spread to other cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's ״משרת״ lesson should apply to all prohibitions, just like the רבנן's.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because היתר מצטרף לאיסור is also taught in חטאת, the rule stays limited to נזיר and חטאת.

steps.title: Where is the sin-offering source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the נזיר source is ״משרת״ and asks what the חטאת source is.
steps.simpleTranslation: נזיר is what we said. What is the source for חטאת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants to see the second verse that רב אשי relied on. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's answer only works if there really is a חטאת verse teaching the same idea. The נזיר source is already known from ״משרת״. Now the גמרא asks for the חטאת source.

keyTerms.meaning: What we already said.
What is it?

phrases.english: Nazir: that which we said.
phrases.notes: He means the word ״משרת״ from earlier.

phrases.english: Sin-offering: what is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: נָזִיר הָא דַּאֲמַרַן חַטָּאת מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the second verse that רב אשי's answer needs.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which verse teaches the joining rule for חטאת

steps.title: The ברייתא on ״כל אשר יגע בבשרה יקדש״
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that food touching the חטאת takes on its status only once it absorbs from the חטאת's flesh. This is the חטאת source.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: "Anything that touches its flesh shall become holy." You might think this applies even if it did not absorb. So the verse says "in its flesh": only once it has absorbed into its flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show the חטאת source. Food that absorbs from the חטאת takes on its holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״בבשרה״ shows that simple touching is not enough; the food must absorb from the חטאת. Once permitted food absorbs from the חטאת, it takes on the חטאת's rules. This is the second verse that, together with נזיר, keeps the joining rule from spreading to other cases.

keyTerms.meaning: It becomes holy and takes on the status of the offering.
You might have thought.
Therefore the verse says.
That it absorbs.

steps.whatToRemember: The joining rule appears in two places: נזיר (״משרת״) and חטאת (״בבשרה״). Since it is taught twice, it cannot be spread to the rest of the Torah.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
"Anything that touches its flesh shall become holy."
You might think: even if it did not absorb.
So the verse says: "in its flesh,"
only once it absorbs into its flesh.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יִגַּע בִּבְשָׂרָהּ יִקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חטאת source is ״בבשרה״: food takes on the חטאת's holiness only once it absorbs from it.

steps.title: The food becomes just like the חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: ״יקדש״ means the touching food gets the same status as the חטאת. If the חטאת is disqualified, so is the food. If it is valid, the food is eaten under the חטאת's strict rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'It shall become holy' means it becomes just like the חטאת. If the חטאת is disqualified, the food is disqualified too. If the חטאת is valid, the food must be eaten under the stricter rules of the חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from the last step. It explains exactly what status the ordinary food takes on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ordinary food did not start out holy. It became like the חטאת only because it absorbed from it. That is the חטאת version of היתר מצטרף לאיסור, so now there are two sources for the idea: נזיר and חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: It shall become holy (the word in the פסוק)
Like it, meaning the same status as the חטאת
Disqualified
According to its strictest rules

steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the second source. רב אשי's claim that the rule cannot spread depends on there being two sources that teach the same idea.

phrases.english: "Shall become holy" means to be like it,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:20. 'It' is the חטאת meat that the food touched.

phrases.english: so that if it is disqualified, the food becomes disqualified,
and if it is valid,
it is eaten according to its strictest rules.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in step 11, which is the answer to step 10's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The food absorbs from the חטאת and takes on its full status, so היתר מצטרף לאיסור is also taught by חטאת.

steps.title: The רבנן say both sources are needed
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן reply that neither source could have been learned from the other. נזיר cannot be learned from holy things, and חטאת cannot be learned from נזיר because נזיר is unusually strict. So both verses are needed, and the rule can still spread to the whole Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן say both are needed. If the Torah wrote it only by חטאת, I would say נזיר cannot be learned from it, because we don't learn נזיר from holy things. If the Torah wrote it only by נזיר, I would say we can't learn from נזיר, because its prohibition is strict: even a grape seed is forbidden to him. So חטאת could not be learned from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן defend themselves against רב אשי's answer from step 9. They argue that the two sources are not extra, because each one teaches something the other could not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that 'two verses teaching the same thing don't spread' applies only when one verse could have been learned from the other. The רבנן show that each case has its own special feature that would block learning from it. So the two verses are not repeating each other, and spreading the rule is still allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: They are needed, meaning each verse teaches something the other could not
I would have thought
Holy things, like קרבנות
We learn (one law from another)
Grape seed

steps.confusionAlert: The רבנן are not saying the rule applies only to נזיר and חטאת. They argue that because both verses are needed, the rule CAN spread to the whole Torah.

phrases.english: And the רבנן would say: both are needed,
for if the Merciful One had written it only by חטאת,
I would have said:
נזיר cannot be learned from it,
because we do not learn נזיר from holy things.
And if the Merciful One had written it only by נזיר,
I would have said:
we do not learn from נזיר,
because his prohibition is strict,
since even a grape seed is forbidden to him,
therefore חטאת cannot be learned from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on רב אשי's step 9 answer by showing the two sources are not repeats.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without both verses, we would think the rule applies only to whichever case was written.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both verses are needed, so they are not 'two verses teaching one thing,' and the rule can spread to the whole Torah.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the חטאת verse is not needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that only the נזיר verse was needed. True, נזיר cannot be learned from חטאת. But חטאת could have been learned from נזיר, since the רבנן themselves learn all the Torah's prohibitions from נזיר. So the two verses teach one idea, and the rule cannot spread.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא would say: why are both needed? Fine, if the Torah wrote only חטאת, we could not learn נזיר from it, because we don't learn ordinary things from holy things. But the Torah could have written it only by נזיר, and we would learn חטאת from it. After all, you learn all the prohibitions in the Torah from נזיר!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא knocks down the second half of the רבנן's argument. He shows that חטאת could have been learned from נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן said נזיר is too strict to learn from. But the רבנן themselves take the נזיר lesson of טעם כעיקר from ״משרת״ and apply it to all of the Torah, so they do learn from נזיר. That makes the חטאת verse extra, and the two verses become 'two verses teaching one thing,' which cannot spread.

keyTerms.meaning: Why are they needed?
Granted, this part makes sense
Ordinary, non-holy things
We learn

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's position: נזיר cannot be learned from חטאת, but חטאת can be learned from נזיר. So one of the two sources is extra, and היתר מצטרף לאיסור stays limited to those cases.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא is using the רבנן's own way of learning against them: they learn all prohibitions from נזיר, so they cannot claim that nothing can be learned from נזיר.

phrases.english: And רבי עקיבא would say to you:
Why are both needed?
Granted, if the Merciful One had written only חטאת,
נזיר would not be learned from it,
since we do not learn ordinary things from holy things.
But let the Merciful One write it only by נזיר,
and חטאת would be learned from it,
for after all, all the prohibitions in the Torah
they learn from נזיר.
phrases.notes: This points back to step 8: the רבנן spread the lesson of ״משרת״, taste counting like the food, from נזיר to all of the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: ורבי עקיבא אמר לך למאי צריכי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the second half of the רבנן's צריכותא in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the claim that חטאת could not be learned from נזיר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The רבנן themselves learn all prohibitions from נזיר, so נזיר's strictness does not stop us from learning from it.

steps.title: The רבנן: each verse teaches a different rule
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer רבי עקיבא's point by giving each verse its own job. The חטאת verse teaches that permitted food joins with forbidden food, and this stays limited to holy things. ״משרת״ teaches טעם כעיקר, which spreads to all prohibitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן would say: the חטאת verse teaches that permitted food joins with forbidden food. We cannot apply that to ordinary food, because we don't learn ordinary things from holy things. ״משרת״ teaches that the taste of a forbidden food counts like the food itself. From there you learn this for all the Torah's prohibitions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how the רבנן avoid the problem of 'two verses teaching one idea.' They say the two verses teach two different rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא had argued that the חטאת verse adds nothing new. The רבנן answer that it teaches its own rule, that permitted food joins with forbidden food, and that rule stays inside holy things. That leaves ״משרת״ free to teach טעם כעיקר alone, so it can be applied to every prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: A permitted food joins with a forbidden food to make up the amount needed for punishment
The taste of a forbidden food counts just like the forbidden food itself
Ordinary food that is not holy
Holy things, such as קרבנות

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two rules. 'Permitted joins with forbidden' is about making up the amount needed. טעם כעיקר is about taste counting like the food itself. For the רבנן, only טעם כעיקר spreads to the whole Torah.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis would say to you:
The sin-offering verse teaches that permitted food combines with forbidden food,
and we do not learn ordinary food from holy things.
And "soaked" teaches that taste counts like the actual substance,

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן אַתָּה דָּן לְכׇל אִיסּוּרִין שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: from here you learn it for all prohibitions in the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the רבנן against רבי עקיבא's claim in step 14 that the two verses teach one idea.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives each verse a different teaching, so they are no longer two verses teaching one idea
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both verses teach the same thing, so nothing can be learned from them for other cases
steps.terutzMaskana: The חטאת verse teaches that permitted joins with forbidden, limited to holy things. ״משרת״ teaches טעם כעיקר for the whole Torah.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: both verses teach one idea, so they cannot spread
steps.stepSummary: For רבי עקיבא, both verses teach that permitted food joins with forbidden food. They are two verses teaching one idea, and such verses do not teach other cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how does רבי עקיבא see it? Both verses teach that permitted food joins with forbidden food. So they are two verses that teach the same thing, and any two verses that teach the same thing cannot be used to learn other cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי עקיבא does not accept the רבנן's split. He reads ״משרת״ as teaching the same rule as the חטאת verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole argument depends on what ״משרת״ teaches. For רבי עקיבא it teaches 'permitted joins with forbidden,' the same as the חטאת verse. Two verses teaching one idea show that the rule is limited to those cases, so it does not spread to the rest of the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them
Two verses that teach the same idea
They do not teach other cases

steps.whatToRemember: The argument comes down to what ״משרת״ teaches. The רבנן say טעם כעיקר, so the rule spreads to the whole Torah. רבי עקיבא says permitted joins with forbidden, the same as the חטאת verse, so the rule does not spread.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the rule of 'two verses teaching one idea' in action. Whether a rule spreads to the whole Torah depends on whether the two verses really overlap.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking how רבי עקיבא would answer the רבנן.

phrases.english: Both verses teach that permitted food combines with forbidden food,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָווּ לְהוּ שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִין הַבָּאִין כְּאֶחָד,
phrases.english: so they are two verses that come as one,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִין הַבָּאִים כְּאֶחָד — אֵין מְלַמְּדִין.
phrases.english: and any two verses that come as one do not teach other cases.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, תַּרְוַיְיהוּ לְהֶיתֵּר מִצְטָרֵף לְאִיסּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the רבנן's split in step 15 by reading both verses as teaching the same rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that ״משרת״ teaches טעם כעיקר separately
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: For רבי עקיבא, ״משרת״ teaches permitted joins with forbidden, the same as the חטאת verse, so the two verses overlap

steps.title: רב אשי: why would רבי עקיבא need a verse to join two forbidden foods?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks רב כהנא about a ברייתא. It uses a verse to teach that a נזיר's forbidden foods join together. But for רבי עקיבא, even permitted food joins with forbidden food, so the verse seems unneeded.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to רב כהנא: what about this ברייתא? The verse 'anything made from the grapevine' teaches that a נזיר's forbidden foods join together. But for רבי עקיבא, if even a permitted food joins with a forbidden one, why would we need a verse to say that two forbidden foods join?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי raises a new challenge against רבי עקיבא. If his rule is right, a verse in a ברייתא seems to teach something we already knew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Logically, two forbidden foods should join even more easily than a permitted food and a forbidden one. Since רבי עקיבא already says permitted joins with forbidden for a נזיר, the ברייתא's verse looks unnecessary. This is a קל וחומר-style attack: the bigger rule should already include the smaller one.

keyTerms.meaning: That which is taught in a ברייתא
They join with each other to make up the amount
Now that
Is it even needed?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Rav Kahana:
But what about that which is taught in a baraita:
"Anything that is made of the grapevine"
teaches about the prohibitions of a nazirite
that they combine with each other,
according to Rabbi Akiva,

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא יֵשׁ לוֹמַר הֶיתֵּר מִצְטָרֵף לְאִיסּוּר,
phrases.english: now that one can say permitted food combines with forbidden food,
is it even necessary to teach that forbidden combines with forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא: אֶלָּא הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רבי עקיבא's position from step 16 and challenges it from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's view that, for a נזיר, permitted food joins with forbidden food
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even permitted food joins with forbidden food, then two forbidden foods should obviously join. So the ברייתא's verse teaching this would be unneeded.

steps.title: Forbidden foods join even when eaten one after the other
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers רב אשי. Permitted food joins with forbidden food only when they are eaten at the same time. Two forbidden foods join even when eaten one after the other, so the ברייתא's verse teaches a new rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Permitted food joins with forbidden food only when eaten at the same time. Forbidden food joins with forbidden food even when eaten one after the other.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers רב אשי's question from the last step. He shows that the ברייתא's verse is not extra after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי thought: if permitted food can join with forbidden food, then two forbidden foods should obviously join, so why would we need a verse? רב כהנא explains that the two kinds of joining work differently. Permitted food joins only when it is mixed and eaten together, but the verse teaches that two of a נזיר's forbidden foods join even when they are eaten separately, one after the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted food joining with forbidden food to make up the amount needed for punishment
One forbidden food joining with another forbidden food
At the same time, eaten together
One after the other, eaten separately

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי עקיבא there are two kinds of joining. היתר לאיסור works only when the foods are eaten together. איסור לאיסור works even when they are eaten one after the other. That is why the ברייתא still needs its verse.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the second rule is just a repeat of the first. The new point is about timing: two forbidden foods join even when they are not eaten together.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב כהנא answering רב אשי's question from the last step.

phrases.english: Permitted with forbidden: only at the same time,

phrases.aramaic: אִיסּוּר לְאִיסּוּר — אֲפִילּוּ בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה.
phrases.english: forbidden with forbidden: even one after the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הֶיתֵּר לְאִיסּוּר — בְּבַת אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's question in step 17 about why the ברייתא's verse is needed for רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two rules apart. They differ in timing, so the verse teaches something new.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since even permitted food joins with forbidden food, the verse teaching that forbidden foods join seemed to add nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Permitted food joins only when eaten together. Forbidden foods join even when eaten one after the other, and this second rule needs the verse.

steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new question about how רבי שמעון's view fits this topic. The question continues past this point.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting a new question about רבי שמעון's opinion, and the rest of the question comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the discussion focused on the רבנן and רבי עקיבא. The words ״ורבי שמעון״ shift attention to a third opinion. The גמרא is about to ask how רבי שמעון handles this teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: And רבי שמעון: the opening of a question about his view

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon,
